ios.desc:
Genki Studio turns your iPad into a portable monitor and professional video capture and presentation device. Connect your Genki ShadowCast or any compatible USB UVC input device to start using your iPad as a portable monitor for your gaming console, PC, digital camera, small board computer, or microscope. Record the input at maximum quality and save the media file directly to your iPad or an external SSD to save storage space on your iPad. With external monitor support, your iPad can output full-screen content to another external display via AirPlay or USB-C to HDMI/DisplayPort adapters while continuing recording to your iPad, while using Apple Pencil markup for a quick presentation. 

Highlights of this app:
· Connect your Genki ShadowCast or any compatible USB UVC input device to your iPad.
· Capture images or videos with audio with maximum quality, to your iPad storage or directly to an external storage device like a portable SSD. 
· Fully compatible with Stage Manager and Multitasking features of the iPad, enjoy music or play a video on your iPad with Genki Studio app running simultaneously.
· Support for Fractional Frame rates, Grid and Ratio Overlay for professional monitoring.
· Mark Up with Apple Pencil support lets you scribble on the screen. 
· External Display support to output clean video image to AirPlay or a wired connection, while continuing recording to your iPad at the same time. Turn your iPad into a portable notepad with Apple Pencil support for live events.
· iPadOS menu bar, keyboard shortcuts and game controller support for various app functions allows you to quickly capture the moment.
· Optimized for accessibility with VoiceOver support.

* Connecting to UVC devices requires a compatible model of iPad. Requires additional accessories; this app supports Genki ShadowCast, and any other input device that conform with UVC (USB Video Class) standards. Appropriate USB-C adapters, docks, or hubs are required for some devices or configurations. Multitasking features require a compatible model of iPad. Connecting to External Displays wirelessly requires AirPlay 2-enabled TVs, streaming boxes or sticks, or a compatible Mac with the latest macOS update installed; also, using a non-Genki ShadowCast capture product will have an added Genki logo watermark on the clean video output Image.

quotes.text:
If you already carry a an iPad in your laptop bag, but use Windows or Linux on your laptop, you can use the iPad as an external monitor using:

- a cheap HDMI USB capture device ($5 from Temu)

- a short HDMI cable to connect that to your laptop's HDMI output

- a USB to lightning or USB to type C adapter (depending on your iPad model)

- a free app to display the UVC camera input full screen, e.g. https://apps.apple.com/us/app/genki-studio/id6466343285

This isn't quite as convenient, but it's not much extra weight to throw in your bag.

My son uses the Genki Studio app on his iPad. It works well enough without payment.

https://apps.apple.com/us/app/genki-studio/id6466343285

I don't know how Orion compares.

The home page says the one-time IAP unlocks 'AI-powered 4k upscaling', which sounds useful.
quotes.story_title: Using a laptop as an HDMI monitor for an SBC
